direction: Calm, warm, confident educator. One continuous read, conversational pace (~150 wpm). Let sentences run into each other; small natural breaths, no robotic gaps. Slight lift on 'Now watch', settle down on the key line.

lines.text: This heart is in sinus rhythm, but look how long it takes from each spike to the end of its T wave.
That's a long QT. The ventricles take longer than normal to reset, and that leaves them vulnerable.
Now watch what happens in torsades de pointes.
A fast ventricular rhythm twists around the baseline, the complexes growing and shrinking like a ribbon.
It can stop on its own, or turn into V-fib.
If it keeps going, defibrillate right away, pulse or not, and start CPR if there's no pulse. IV magnesium helps stop it coming back.
Practice it on ACLSMED Sim. ACLSmed dot com.
